headline: Statistical methods refine GWAS inference from summary data and censored biomarkers
label: Statistical Inference In Gwas
summary: Summary-statistic estimators and censoring-aware models address inference when individual-level data or complete biomarker measurements are unavailable.
synthesis: The dominant thread here is statistical estimation under data constraints. FastHer recovers local heritability from GWAS summary statistics and LD matrices using a single eigen-decomposition, matching HEELS and GREML accuracy, so individual-level data are not required. A second paper addresses measurement quality, reporting X-chromosome telomere length primers and a feedforward neural network age-prediction tool in Han individuals, with a proposed telomere shortening rate. A third compares linear, Tobit, Cox and logistic models for below-limit-of-detection biomarkers in GWAS by simulation and proposes a two-step Linear-Tobit scheme. What is new is explicit attention to censored biomarker values and assay precision within GWAS-scale association frameworks, extending beyond aggregate summary-level estimators.
